GameConditionDef.label: the cats keeping watch
GameConditionDef.description: The cats sit with the graves, and the rats have gone.

texts.li: The {BEAST} has lain down across the way in and will not move. Whoever goes near her hears a question in no voice at all: "{TALE}" She is waiting for an answer.

[age0] The {BEAST} has lain down across the way into the camp, like a cat on a cairn, and will not move. Whoever goes near her hears a question in no voice at all: "{TALE}" She is waiting for an answer.

[age1] The {BEAST} has lain down across the gate, still as the carvings at a crypt door, and will not move. Whoever goes near her hears a question in no voice at all: "{TALE}" She is waiting for an answer.

[age2] The {BEAST} has lain down across the doorway and will not move, and the colony's cats sit in a row behind her. Whoever goes near her hears a question in no voice at all: "{TALE}" She is waiting for an answer.

[age3] The {BEAST} has lain down across the way in, as the old stories put the Sphinx at the door, and will not move. Whoever goes near her hears a question in no voice at all: "{TALE}" She is waiting for an answer.

li.label: Send {A_nameDef}, the sharpest wits here
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} walks out to the {BEAST} to answer her.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} walks out to the {BEAST} to answer her.

li.label: Send {B_nameDef}, who talks best
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} walks out to the {BEAST} to answer her.
li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} walks out to the {BEAST} to answer her.

li.label: Let her lie there
li.outcome: Nobody goes out to her. The {BEAST} lies across the way a while longer, then gets up and walks back to the graves.

li.label: answered the great cat
li.description: I stood in front of her and answered her riddle, and she got up and pressed her head under my hand. She walks with me now.

li.label: gave the great cat a wrong answer
li.description: I got her riddle wrong, and she looked at me as if she had known all along that I would.

li.label: a grave kept
li.description: Someone sat the first night by the new grave, or a cat keeps it still and won't come away. Whoever lies there is in good keeping.

li.label: saw the dead stand up
li.description: Figures wrapped in grey cloth stood up out of the ground among the graves, slow and silent. They were facing the raiders, but they weren't ours anymore.

HediffDef.label: wrapped dead
HediffDef.description: Wrapped in grey cloth from head to foot, it stood up out of the ground among the graves. It doesn't breathe, and it won't leave the graves.

plain.li: Sleep well, {DEAD}, {GOD} keeps the door tonight.
We sit with you this first night, {DEAD}, as {GOD} asks of us.
The cat will stay when I go, {DEAD}, so you won't be alone.
Rest whole, {DEAD}, and let nothing in the dark come near you.
There's a cat on {DEAD}'s grave, and it won't come away.
Leave the cat be, it's keeping {DEAD} company.
My gran used to say a cat on a new grave means the dead are well kept.
[own] Our cat hasn't left {DEAD}'s grave all day.
[stray] Where did that cat come from, and why did it go straight to {DEAD}?
[rise] The dead are standing up out of the graves, keep away from them.
[rise] They're wrapped like the old dead, and they're facing the raiders.
[rise] Don't go near the graves, whatever's standing there isn't ours anymore.
